title.zh: 关西家庭旅行：大阪、奈良、京都与宇治
title.en: Kansai Family Trip — Osaka, Nara, Kyoto & Uji

subtitle.zh: 和妈妈、妹妹一起，从奈良的鹿走到宇治的河边
subtitle.en: With Mom and my sister, from Nara's deer to the riverside in Uji

intro.zh: 带妈妈和妹妹从大阪出发，去奈良看鹿、在京都找回丢失的钱包，再沿宇治川慢慢走。六天很充实，也有几段真正慢下来的时光。
intro.en: Mom, my sister and I started in Osaka, met the deer in Nara, found a lost wallet in Kyoto, and slowed down beside the Uji River. Six full days, with room to breathe.

paragraphs.zh: 11 月 10 日，和妈妈、妹妹从浦东出发，飞往大阪关西机场。机场的一杯咖啡，是这趟六天家庭旅行的开场。
paragraphs.en: On November 10, Mom, my sister and I flew from Pudong to Kansai Airport. A coffee at the airport marked the beginning of our six days together.

caption.zh: 从浦东启程。
caption.en: Leaving Pudong together.

paragraphs.zh: 晚上到心斋桥一带，当然也想和格力高广告牌合影。道顿堀的霓虹灯把第一晚照得很热闹；一兰拉面是晚餐，三个人花了 6,000 日元。
paragraphs.en: That evening we headed to Shinsaibashi for the familiar Glico-billboard photo. Dōtonbori's neon made our first night lively; dinner at Ichiran cost ¥6,000 for the three of us.

caption.zh: 三个人的一兰晚餐，给第一晚垫个底。
caption.en: Ichiran for three, to start our first evening.

caption.zh: 运河与街巷，各有各的热闹。
caption.en: Along the canal and in the lanes, two sides of Osaka after dark.

paragraphs.zh: 饭后在 ABC Mart 买鞋花了 8,000 日元，又在大国药妆花了 20,000 日元。住大阪的 Fresa Inn Kitahama，离心斋桥约两站地铁。
paragraphs.en: After dinner, I bought shoes at ABC Mart for ¥8,000 and we spent ¥20,000 at Daikoku Drug. We stayed at Fresa Inn Kitahama, about two metro stops from Shinsaibashi.

paragraphs.zh: 早餐在 Doutor Coffee 解决，再从大阪坐近铁，约 40 分钟到奈良站。先去兴福寺，门票每人 500 日元；走进奈良公园，鹿已经不怎么怕人了，公园里看鹿不用门票。
paragraphs.en: We had breakfast at Doutor Coffee and took the Kintetsu train from Osaka, reaching Nara Station in about 40 minutes. Kōfuku-ji was ¥500 each; the deer in free-to-enter Nara Park seemed entirely unafraid of us.

caption.zh: 奈良的第一站，先看寺院的屋檐。
caption.en: Our first stop in Nara, beneath the temple roofs.

caption.zh: 一只歇着，一只走近，鹿有自己的节奏。
caption.en: One resting, one coming closer—the deer set their own pace.

paragraphs.zh: 奈良国立博物馆的正仓院展每人 2,200 日元，笔记里记下了奈良历史和神武天皇。馆外仍然到处是鹿。它们会主动来找鹿饼，但拿着饼不要在雄鹿面前晃。
paragraphs.en: The Shōsōin Exhibition at Nara National Museum cost ¥2,200 each; I noted its Nara history and Emperor Jimmu exhibits. Deer were everywhere outside too. They come right up for crackers, but I learned not to wave a cracker in front of a stag.

caption.zh: 从展厅出来，奈良仍然由鹿带路。
caption.en: Even outside the museum, the deer kept us company.

paragraphs.zh: 午餐是东大寺旁边的牛肉饭，之后去东大寺，看南大门和大佛殿；也在园里留下一张全家合影。
paragraphs.en: Lunch was beef rice beside Tōdai-ji. We went on to the Great South Gate and Great Buddha Hall and took a family photograph in the gardens.

caption.zh: 牛肉饭、配汤和小菜，吃完再继续走。
caption.en: Beef rice, soup and little sides before we carried on.

caption.zh: 一路抬头看木构与屋檐，东大寺的尺度很有气势。
caption.en: Timber and sweeping roofs gave the walk through Tōdai-ji its scale.

caption.zh: 风景之外，把我们三个人也装进照片。
caption.en: Not just the scenery—a frame for the three of us.

caption.zh: 大佛殿前，游人衬出了殿堂的高大。
caption.en: Visitors in front of the Great Buddha Hall put its size in perspective.

caption.zh: 池边和林间，都有鹿安安静静地待着。
caption.en: Beside the pond and among the trees, the deer had found quiet spots.

caption.zh: 庭园里的石径，给寺院这一段收个尾。
caption.en: A garden path to close this part of the temple walk.

paragraphs.zh: 走过春日大社，林间石灯笼和鹿一路相伴。若草山门票每人 150 日元；在山坡上等到夕阳，下山的光线真美。这是全程最治愈的一天。
paragraphs.en: We walked through Kasuga Taisha among stone lanterns and deer. Mount Wakakusa cost ¥150 each; we stayed for the sunset, and the light on the way down was beautiful. It was the most restorative day of the trip.

caption.zh: 草地上散着鹿，林间的光也慢了下来。
caption.en: Deer dotted the grass as the light softened among the trees.

paragraphs.zh: 整理照片时查了春日大社的介绍：境内约有三千座奉纳灯笼，建筑还通过每二十年一次的「式年造替」进行修缮、更新。再看这些沿林间小径排开的石灯笼，才意识到当天随手拍下的，不只是好看的风景，也是长久积累下来的祈愿。
paragraphs.en: While sorting the photos, I read that Kasuga Taisha has around 3,000 donated lanterns, and that its buildings are repaired and renewed through the Shikinen Zotai ceremony every twenty years. Looking again at those stone lanterns along the wooded paths, I saw more than a pretty scene: they were wishes accumulated over generations.

caption.zh: 石灯笼与树影，沿着小径一层层展开。
caption.en: Stone lanterns and tree shadows receded along the path.

caption.zh: 从树林的绿色里，走到神社的朱红色前。
caption.en: From the green of the woods to the shrine's vermilion.

caption.zh: 山坡上，时间终于慢下来。
caption.en: Up on the hillside, the day finally slowed down.

caption.zh: 天色渐晚，鹿还留在草坡上。
caption.en: As the sun went down, the deer were still on the grass.

caption.zh: 从金色天光等到太阳落下，奈良这一天舍不得结束。
caption.en: From golden light to the setting sun, a Nara day we did not want to end.

paragraphs.zh: 记得去车站方向的末班车是 16:45，步行到车站约需 20 分钟。回到大阪难波，Okini 自助烤肉三人约 13,000 日元。后来去 Bic Camera 买电子产品：MacBook 和耳机约 96,000 日元；笔记里写着笔记本便宜 13,000、耳机便宜 200。日版笔记本默认日式键盘，想要美式键盘一定要指定 US Keyboard。
paragraphs.en: My note says the last bus toward the station was at 16:45 and the walk to the station took around 20 minutes. Back in Namba, Okini all-you-can-eat barbecue cost about ¥13,000 for three. At Bic Camera we bought electronics: a MacBook and headphones for about ¥96,000; my note records savings of 13,000 on the laptop and 200 on the headphones, without a comparison basis. Japanese models have a Japanese keyboard layout, so we had to request a US Keyboard.

paragraphs.zh: 又在 Doutor Coffee 吃过早餐，去大阪城。地铁站离天守阁还有一段路；天守阁门票每人 600 日元，逛下来约两小时。提前买票可以少排队。护城河和城墙，远看近看都很有气势。
paragraphs.en: Another Doutor Coffee breakfast, then Osaka Castle. The keep was a fair walk from the station; admission was ¥600 each and our visit took about two hours. Buying tickets ahead can save the queue. The moat and walls looked imposing from every angle.

caption.zh: 先绕过护城河，才走近天守阁。
caption.en: We walked along the moat before reaching the keep.

paragraphs.zh: 后来补看大阪城的历史，才分清眼前建筑的年代：如今的天守阁是第三代，1931 年靠市民捐款重建，从落成起就是博物馆；现存的石垣、护城河等遗构则属于德川时代及以后。照片里看似同一座城，其实叠着不同年代的故事。
paragraphs.en: Reading the castle's history afterward helped me separate its layers. Today's keep is the third incarnation, rebuilt in 1931 with donations from Osaka residents and used as a museum from the start. The surviving stone walls, moats and other historic structures date from the Tokugawa period onward. What looks like one castle in the photos holds several different eras.

caption.zh: 同一座天守阁，云层与蓝天各留一面。
caption.en: The same keep, framed once by clouds and once by blue sky.

caption.zh: 从高处回望大阪与公园。
caption.en: Looking back across Osaka and the park from above.

caption.zh: 天守阁前，我们三个人也留了一张合影。
caption.en: A photograph of the three of us in front of the castle keep.

paragraphs.zh: 午餐在大阪城外的罗森随便吃了点。接着去难波八坂神社，那张张着大嘴的狮子殿很难忘；再走到通天阁和新世界，招牌挤在一起。
paragraphs.en: Lunch was a quick stop at the Lawson outside the castle. Then we visited Namba Yasaka Shrine and its unforgettable open-mouthed lion hall, before heading to Tsūtenkaku and Shinsekai, where the signs crowd the street.

paragraphs.zh: 这张「大嘴」也值得补一笔：大阪观光局介绍，难波八坂神社的狮子造型建筑高约 12 米、宽约 11 米、深约 10 米。把这些数字和我们的合影放在一起看，才更容易理解当时为什么一眼就记住了它。
paragraphs.en: That enormous mouth deserves a little background too. Osaka's tourism bureau gives the lion-head structure's dimensions as about 12 metres high, 11 metres wide and 10 metres deep. Put those numbers beside our family photo and it is easy to see why it made such an immediate impression.

caption.zh: 正面与侧面，这张大嘴都很抢眼。
caption.en: Head-on or from the side, that enormous mouth stole the scene.

caption.zh: 看过大狮子，再停下来看看一排排绘马。
caption.en: After the lion hall, a pause by the rows of votive plaques.

caption.zh: 站在狮子殿前，才更看得出它有多大。
caption.en: Standing in front of the lion hall gave it a human scale.

caption.zh: 通天阁就在新世界街道的尽头。
caption.en: Tsūtenkaku at the far end of Shinsekai.

paragraphs.zh: 下午在梅田扫货：Lucua 的 Lululemon 花了 90,000 日元；友都八喜户外区只逛没买；Lucua 1100 女装两笔分别是 30,000 和 60,000 日元。大丸百货 13 楼买了 2,000 日元的任天堂小礼物，又在阪急百货 4 楼花 20,000 日元代购鬼冢虎。
paragraphs.en: Our Umeda shopping run began with ¥90,000 at Lululemon in Lucua. We browsed Yodobashi's outdoor section without buying anything, then spent ¥30,000 and ¥60,000 on womenswear at Lucua 1100. We picked up ¥2,000 of small Nintendo gifts on Daimaru's 13th floor and made a ¥20,000 Onitsuka Tiger proxy purchase on Hankyu's fourth floor.

paragraphs.zh: 晚餐在阪急百货 12 楼吃猪排，三人约 4,500 日元，真的好吃！晚上又在堂吉诃德买药妆，约 27,000 日元。
paragraphs.en: Dinner was pork cutlet on Hankyu's 12th floor—really good, and about ¥4,500 for the three of us. We finished with around ¥27,000 of pharmacy and beauty shopping at Don Quijote.

caption.zh: 忙了一整天，这顿猪排很合心意。
caption.en: After a busy day, that pork cutlet really hit the spot.

paragraphs.zh: 在 Doutor Coffee 吃过早餐，从大阪坐电车到京都，落脚四条大宫的 Travelodge。先逛锦市场，午餐就吃市场里的各样小吃。走到鸭川边拍照，一家人也在河边合影。
paragraphs.en: After breakfast at Doutor Coffee we took the train from Osaka to Kyoto and settled at Travelodge in Shijo-Omiya. We browsed Nishiki Market, eating a mix of market snacks for lunch, then took photos by the Kamo River together.

caption.zh: 市场这一带，也藏着让人驻足的小小神社。
caption.en: Around the market, a small shrine offered another place to pause.

caption.zh: 河对岸的房子和沿岸的秋色，换个方向又是一幅画。
caption.en: Riverside buildings and autumn trees, seen from two directions.

caption.zh: 鸭川边的合影，三个人一个都不能少。
caption.en: By the Kamo River, with all three of us in the frame.

paragraphs.zh: 花见小路也拍了照；这里可以租和服，我们没有租。沿着八坂神社、二年坂和三年坂慢慢逛，街巷里抬头就能看见塔。
paragraphs.en: We took photos on Hanamikoji, though we skipped the kimono rental. Then we wandered around Yasaka Shrine, Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, looking up to find a pagoda above the streets.

caption.zh: 京都的街巷，适合走走停停。
caption.en: Kyoto's lanes made it easy to pause along the way.

caption.zh: 沿街巷往前走，塔尖从屋顶之间露出来。
caption.en: Further along the lane, a pagoda rose between the roofs.

caption.zh: 八坂神社里，鸟居与灯笼把视线留住。
caption.en: At Yasaka Shrine, the torii and lanterns caught our eye.

caption.zh: 朱红门楼之后，继续寻找街巷里的塔。
caption.en: Beyond the vermilion gate, another glimpse of the pagoda in the lanes.

paragraphs.zh: 清水寺的夜间参拜每人 500 日元。偏偏在这里弄丢了钱包，又奇迹般找了回来——比风景更让人记得牢的，就是这一场虚惊。
paragraphs.en: Nighttime admission to Kiyomizu-dera was ¥500 each. This was where we lost a wallet and, miraculously, found it again. That moment of panic and relief became the story we remember most.

caption.zh: 清水寺红色的门，见证了这场虚惊。
caption.en: Kiyomizu-dera's red gates framed the wallet scare.

caption.zh: 清水寺石阶前，一家人都在镜头里。
caption.en: All three of us together by the temple steps.

caption.zh: 继续往里走，塔与屋檐渐渐映入眼帘。
caption.en: Further inside, the pagoda came into view above the roofs.

caption.zh: 天色渐暗，京都塔亮了起来。
caption.en: The light faded and Kyoto Tower came on.

caption.zh: 到京都站时，塔已经亮在夜色里。
caption.en: By the time we reached Kyoto Station, the tower was bright against the night.

paragraphs.zh: 晚餐到京都站的 Musashi 吃旋转寿司，鱼生选择比较多，不喜欢生鱼片的人可能不合适。回程逛优衣库花了 5,000 日元：妹妹买内搭，妈妈买羽绒背心，最后回 Travelodge Shijo Omiya。
paragraphs.en: At Kyoto Station we had conveyor-belt sushi at Musashi. There was plenty of raw fish, so I would not pick it for someone who dislikes sashimi. On the way back, my sister bought base layers and Mom a down vest at Uniqlo for ¥5,000 altogether, before we returned to Travelodge Shijo Omiya.

paragraphs.zh: 早餐在 Tully's Coffee，花了 2,000 日元。先去东本愿寺，再到京都站与京都塔合影。之后先到伏见稻荷大社；午餐是不好吃的列车便当，另在神社外的便利店买了些吃的。
paragraphs.en: Breakfast at Tully's Coffee was ¥2,000. We visited Higashi Hongan-ji and took a Kyoto Tower photo at the station. Then we went to Fushimi Inari Taisha first. Lunch was a disappointing train bento, supplemented by a convenience-store stop outside the shrine.

caption.zh: 从四条大宫的住处出发。
caption.en: Leaving our Shijo-Omiya hotel for the day.

caption.zh: 在东本愿寺停下脚步。
caption.en: A pause at Higashi Hongan-ji before moving on.

caption.zh: 寺院边的水道，把天空也收进了画面。
caption.en: Beside the temple, a waterway held a reflection of the sky.

caption.zh: 从寺院到京都塔，背景换了，三个人还在一起。
caption.en: From the temple to Kyoto Tower: a different backdrop, the same three of us.

caption.zh: 出发前，再留一张建筑之间的京都塔。
caption.en: Before leaving, one more view of Kyoto Tower between the buildings.

paragraphs.zh: 补读神社资料才知道，伏见稻荷大社始于 711 年，是日本稻荷神社的总本宫。这里的祈愿从五谷丰登延伸到生意兴隆、家人平安；这也让照片里的朱红色，不再只是一个熟悉的京都地标。
paragraphs.en: The shrine's own history adds another layer: founded in 711, Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of Japan's Inari shrines. Prayers here range from good harvests to business prosperity and the safety of one's family. That gives the vermilion in our photos meaning beyond a familiar Kyoto landmark.

caption.zh: 先在伏见稻荷停留，再往宇治走。
caption.en: A stop at Fushimi Inari before we continued to Uji.

caption.zh: 朱红栏杆与深色屋檐，是神社的另一种层次。
caption.en: Vermilion railings and dark roofs added another layer to the shrine.

paragraphs.zh: 再坐 JR 奈良线前往宇治。比起前几天赶着走的路，这一天最悠闲：在伊藤右卫门和中村藤吉吃了些抹茶小零食，沿宇治桥和宇治川散步拍照，也去了平等院。
paragraphs.en: After Fushimi, we continued to Uji on the JR Nara Line. This was the most leisurely day: matcha snacks from Itohkyuemon and Nakamura Tokichi, a walk and photos along Uji Bridge and the Uji River, and a visit to Byōdō-in.

caption.zh: 先逛抹茶店，把这一站的节奏放慢。
caption.en: A matcha-shop stop set a slower pace for Uji.

caption.zh: 从桥边看到对岸，宇治川把视野一下打开。
caption.en: From the bridge to the opposite bank, the Uji River opened up the view.

caption.zh: 沿河再走一段，不急着赶下一站。
caption.en: A little further along the river, with no hurry to move on.

paragraphs.zh: 平等院的背景也在整理游记时补上：1052 年，藤原赖通把别业改成寺院，次年建成凤凰堂；后来，凤凰堂又成了 10 日元硬币上的图案。补上这段历史，再看当天留下的店铺、河面与庭院入口，宇治就不只是一站抹茶了。
paragraphs.en: I added Byōdō-in's history while putting this diary together: Fujiwara no Yorimichi converted a villa into the temple in 1052, and the Phoenix Hall was completed the following year. The hall later became the design on the 10-yen coin. That bit of history adds another layer to a day our photos remember through shops, water and a garden entrance—there was more to Uji than matcha.

caption.zh: 散步时经过的庭院入口。
caption.en: A garden entrance along the walk.

paragraphs.zh: 乘 JR 奈良线回到京都站，再去四条逛街。始祖鸟只看看，没有买；四条大丸买了 19,000 日元的运动皮鞋、11,000 日元的 Kanebo 精华。
paragraphs.en: We took the JR Nara Line back to Kyoto Station and shopped in Shijo. We browsed Arc'teryx without buying anything; at Daimaru Kyoto we bought sporty leather shoes for ¥19,000 and Kanebo serum for ¥11,000.

paragraphs.zh: 晚餐是大丸百货的炭烧鳗鱼饭，三个人花了 15,000 日元。很好吃，但吃多了会有点腻；下次三个人点两份大的就够了。
paragraphs.en: Dinner was charcoal-grilled eel rice at Daimaru, ¥15,000 for three. Delicious, though a little rich toward the end; two large portions would have been enough for us.

caption.zh: 先把这一整份鳗鱼饭和配菜好好记下来。
caption.en: The whole eel-rice set, little sides included.

caption.zh: 满桌都摆开才发现，下次两份大的真的够了。
caption.en: Seeing the spread explains our note: two large portions next time.

paragraphs.zh: 最后一天，先在酒店附近的咖啡店喝了一杯，再去高岛屋看 Mikimoto。珍珠项链和耳环都很好看，单珠却难买；最后只买到了 7mm 的，记下两笔 80,000 和 60,000 日元。
paragraphs.en: On our last day we started with coffee near the hotel, then went to Mikimoto at Takashimaya. The pearl necklace and earrings were beautiful, but single pearls were hard to find; only the 7 mm size was available. My notes record purchases of ¥80,000 and ¥60,000.

paragraphs.zh: 又到 Lelabo Cafe 打了卡。三杯咖啡和一张合影，给回程前留一点不赶路的时间。
paragraphs.en: We also stopped by Lelabo Cafe. Three cups of coffee and a photo together made room for a little pause before the journey home.

caption.zh: 最后一次一起喝咖啡，给六天留一张合影。
caption.en: One last coffee together, and a photo to remember the six days.

caption.zh: 从店门口到手里的咖啡，给回程前留一点小小的停顿。
caption.en: The doorway and our coffee cups, a small pause before the journey home.

paragraphs.zh: 打车从酒店去京都站，坐 Haruka 特快前往关西机场；笔记里记着车程约 80 分钟、约半小时一班，也记着可以在车上补票、不用提前取票——这是当时的乘车记录，不一定适用于以后。
paragraphs.en: We took a taxi from the hotel to Kyoto Station and boarded the Haruka limited express to Kansai Airport. My travel note says about 80 minutes, departures around every half-hour, and that we could settle the fare on board without collecting tickets in advance; that was our experience then, not current service advice.

caption.zh: 离开前，京都的水道和树影再看一眼。
caption.en: One last look at Kyoto's waterways and trees before leaving.

caption.zh: Haruka 的 Hello Kitty 涂装，给回程添了一点可爱。
caption.en: Haruka's Hello Kitty livery added a playful note to the trip home.

caption.zh: 站里的纪念拍照板，也留下一张到此一游。
caption.en: One more souvenir photo at the station's photo board.

paragraphs.zh: 机场的 Mensho Ramen 午餐花了 5,000 日元，偏贵，味道也一般。下午飞回上海浦东，晚餐是机上点心，已经预订了接机回家。六天里有若草山的夕阳，也有钱包找回来的松一口气；和家人在一起，这些细节才留得最久。
paragraphs.en: Lunch at the airport's Mensho Ramen cost ¥5,000: expensive and only average. We flew back to Shanghai Pudong that afternoon, had a snack on the plane, and took our pre-booked airport pickup home. The Mount Wakakusa sunset and the relief of finding the wallet stayed with me most—little things that last because we were together.

paragraphs.zh: 这些是笔记里写下的门票、餐食和购物价格，不是六天的总花费；没有记下的机票、酒店和车费不计入。每人、三人合计以及约数分别注明，未买的商品不算支出。
paragraphs.en: These are the admission, meal and shopping prices I wrote down, not the cost of the whole trip. Flights, hotels and transport without recorded prices are not included. Per-person prices, group bills and approximate amounts are distinguished; things we did not buy are excluded.
